clue.text: Strangely warm on a ship

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the words warm on a are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Something feels oddly warm aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' scrambles WARMONA.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-o'-war is an old armed sailing warship, so it is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Second one aboard coach journey after son — there seems to be no end to it

definitions.text: there seems to be no end to it

indicators.note: after says the journey word comes behind the son abbreviation

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: aboard says one piece travels inside the vehicle named by the other

parts.note: a coach is a bus
one is the Roman numeral I
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a journey is a trip

explanation.surface: A passenger boards a coach for a seemingly endless trip after their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' makes BIUS; 'after' puts the journey behind S. The definition works because the strip has only one edge and one face.
explanation.definitionFit: A Möbius strip is a one-sided loop with a single continuous edge, so travelling along it you never reach an end.

clue.text: Suggestion from sister without a church

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sister's letters go round the a

parts.note: a religious sister is a nun
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A hint offered by a nun who has no church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking: the sister goes round the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade or hint of meaning, a slight suggestion.

clue.text: Power of art excited Mackintosh

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the words power of art are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Scottish designer Charles Rennie Mackintosh is thrilled by the power of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges POWEROFART. Mackintosh looks like the designer's name, but a mackintosh is a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a rubberised raincoat, and a raincoat can be called a waterproof.

clue.text: Fanatical British papers pursuing artist

indicators.note: pursuing says the papers come behind, following, the earlier pieces

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Zealous British newspapers hound a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' sets B and ID behind RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme or zealous in opinion, like a fanatic.

clue.text: Charlie plays moving love song

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Charlie performs a touching love song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges PLAYS to ALYPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean musical style and a tune in that style.

clue.text: Treatment that can be good for the soul, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Treatment that can be good for the soul, by the sound of it

parts.words: Treatment that can be good for the soul, by the sound of it
parts.note: soul sounds like sole, the underside of the foot, which this kind of foot care treats

explanation.surface: Some therapy that is spiritually uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: The soul is really the sole of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is professional foot care, and the sole is part of the foot it looks after.

clue.text: Strike a light

explanation.surface: An instruction to ignite a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamp is slang for hitting someone, and as a noun it is a lighting fixture.

clue.text: Highly suspicious soldier starts to notice odd incidents daily

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A wary soldier begins noticing strange events every day.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoid describes extreme, often irrational distrust of others.

clue.text: Association football team dropping lead after Ronaldo's finish

indicators.note: finish points to the closing letter of the footballer's name Ronaldo
dropping lead says the first letter slides down from the front to the end of the team name

parts.note: Everton is a Liverpool football club

explanation.surface: The football association team lose their leader after Ronaldo finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping lead' moves the E of EVERTON to the end, giving VERTONE. Everton is a Premier League club from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a connotation, an implied association a word carries.

clue.text: Shot animal left for scavenger essentially

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another in the animal word

parts.note: a beast is an animal

indicators.note: essentially points to the central letter, the essence, of scavenger

explanation.surface: An animal was shot and left for the scavengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts L in place of the E at the heart of scavenger, so BEAST becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast is a shot or explosion, as in a blast from a shotgun.

clue.text: Means to slowly cook 23 bananas with cheese crust

indicators.note: crust says the cheese forms an outer layer around the other letters

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of 23's answer go wild

parts.note: the answer to 23 down is MANIA

explanation.surface: A recipe for a slow-cooked dish of bananas with a cheesy crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like an ingredient but is the anagram signal, making AINMA, and 'crust' wraps the cheese round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bain-marie is a pan of hot water in which food is gently heated, a device for gentle cooking.

clue.text: Derelict found out about interest rates at the start

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the interest word
out suggests the letters of found are put out of order

parts.note: care is interest or concern

indicators.note: at the start points to the opening letter of rates

explanation.surface: An abandoned property is discovered after early rate rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives UNDFO, which 'about' wraps round the interest word; 'at the start' supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncared-for has been neglected and left to decay, like a derelict building.

clue.text: Union's denial broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast says the word is heard over the air, so it is judged by sound

parts.note: not is a word of denial

explanation.surface: A trade union's refusal is put out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot joins two things together, so it is a union, as in tying the knot.

clue.text: Looking up helium and oxygen consumption in part of hospital — it's stored in a repository

indicators.note: in says these letters are set inside the hospital part

parts.note: a ward is a section of a hospital

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue says the helium symbol is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
consumption is use

explanation.surface: A hospital ward's gas usage records end up filed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' turns HE into EH; EH, O and USE make EHOUSE, which goes 'in' WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are warehoused are kept in a large storage building.

clue.text: French pig could be the product of this farm practice

parts.words: French pig could be the product of this
parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer tells you to rotate crop, turning it backwards into porc, French for pig

explanation.surface: A farming technique supposedly yields French pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, and turning CROP round gives PORC, the French for pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Crop rotation is the agricultural method of growing different crops in turn on the same field.

clue.text: Novel mostly perfect, okay, except the last bit — it's hard to read

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are put into a new arrangement
mostly says the word perfect loses its final letter
except the last bit says the word okay is taken without its closing letter

explanation.surface: A nearly perfect novel, fine apart from the ending, is a tough read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' gives PERFEC, 'except the last bit' gives OKA, and 'Novel' scrambles them together.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker face is an expressionless look that gives nothing away, so others cannot tell what the person thinks.

clue.text: Record label close to folding, consider move abroad

parts.note: EMI is a British record company

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the last letter of folding

parts.note: to rate something is to consider or judge it

explanation.surface: As a record company nears collapse, its staff think of relocating overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle in another.

clue.text: Creature, aptly evolved before Manx cat

indicators.note: evolved letters have changed their form, so aptly is rearranged
a Manx cat has no tail, so the cat word loses its last letter

parts.note: puss is a word for a cat

explanation.surface: An animal that has adapted well comes ahead of a tailless cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolved' rearranges APTLY to PLATY; 'Manx' docks PUSS to PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an egg-laying Australian mammal, an animal.

clue.text: 12 put back into race, sure to skirt round northern town

indicators.note: into says the turned piece is placed inside the race word

parts.note: the mile is a race distance in athletics

indicators.note: put back says the letters of 12's answer are written in reverse

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is KNOT

indicators.note: skirt round says the agreement word goes around the northern letter

parts.note: yes is a word of assent, like sure

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to steer a race around a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' makes TONK, which goes 'into' the race; 'skirt round' wraps the assent word round N. Milton Keynes is a new town in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Keynes is a large English new town in Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: I'm returning posh car — or part of car

indicators.note: returning says the letters of I'm go back the other way

parts.note: RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car

explanation.surface: Someone is bringing back a luxury car, or at least a piece of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror is a fitting on a car, the rear-view or wing mirror.

clue.text: Some dubbed pandemic 'potty'

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people called the pandemic crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty looks like an adjective meaning crazy, but here it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpan is a receptacle used as a toilet by a bedridden patient, much like a child's potty.

clue.text: Prat with European holiday home

parts.note: a git is a fool or prat in British slang

explanation.surface: An idiot from Europe owns a holiday cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: Prat and git are both mild British insults for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gîte is a French rural cottage let to holidaymakers.

clue.text: Bouncer using Circle Line after walk

indicators.note: after says the circle and line pieces come behind the walk word

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily
a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman takes the Circle Line on the London Underground after a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncer suggests a nightclub doorman; it is something you bounce on. The Circle Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung mat for jumping on, a thing that makes you bounce.

clue.text: Student not involved in small cigar craze

L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the learner plates on British student drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania is a widespread enthusiasm or obsession, a fad.

clue.text: In the outskirts of Andromeda, with reference to space

the outskirts of says take the first and last letters of Andromeda

parts.note: re means with reference to, concerning

explanation.surface: Something about outer space on the fringes of the Andromeda galaxy.
explanation.walkthrough: Andromeda and space suggest astronomy, but space here is simply room.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is an expanse or region, a space.

clue.text: Relate to a pawnshop losing all content — inevitable after uncle's focus dropped

losing all content says the word pawnshop keeps only its first and last letters

Make subordinate unlimited tea without opening men's toilet first

clue.text: Firedog regularly fanned vitriol before end of election
